```{r}
# =============================================================================
# PDF Immunoreactivity — SHORT-DAY species comparison  (Cx. pipiens vs Cx. quinquefasciatus)
#
# ANALYSIS: Welch's two-sample t-test on BRAIN-AVERAGED values.
#   - The two hemispheres of each brain are averaged to one value per brain
#     (the unit of biological replication), which removes pseudoreplication
#     without needing a mixed model.
#   - Area and CTCF are natural-log transformed prior to testing (variance
#     scaled with the mean; see Methods); differences back-transform to
#     fold-changes. Mean intensity is analyzed on the raw scale.
#   - Welch's t-test does not assume equal variance between species.
#   - Run at threshold 100 (primary) and 75 & 150 (supplemental) to show the
#     result is robust to threshold choice.
#
# INPUT : IHC_long.csv  (96 rows)
# OUTPUT: tables (Welch results, group means, threshold sensitivity) + figures
#         Figures now show significance via a bracket + asterisks (*, **, ***, ns)
#         connecting the two bars, instead of a printed "p = ..." value.
# =============================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ---- load & prepare ---------------------------------------------------------
df <- read.csv("IHC_long.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(df) <- trimws(names(df))

df$species     <- factor(df$species,     levels = c("pipiens","quinquefasciatus"))
df$photoperiod <- factor(df$photoperiod, levels = c("SD","LD"))
df$brain_id    <- factor(df$brain_id)
df$threshold   <- factor(df$threshold,   levels = c("75","100","150"))

if (!"log_area" %in% names(df) || any(is.na(df$log_area))) df$log_area <- log(df$area)
if (!"log_CTCF" %in% names(df) || any(is.na(df$log_CTCF))) df$log_CTCF <- log(df$CTCF)

species_lab <- function(x) factor(ifelse(x=="pipiens","Cx. pipiens","Cx. quinquefasciatus"),
                                  levels = c("Cx. pipiens","Cx. quinquefasciatus"))

# metric registry: key, analysis column (log for area/CTCF), logged?, axis label, title
metrics <- list(
  list(key="area_um2",       col="log_area",       logged=TRUE,  ylab="PDF+ arborization area (um^2)", title="PDF+ arborization area"),
  list(key="CTCF",           col="log_CTCF",       logged=TRUE,  ylab="CTCF (a.u.)",                    title="CTCF"),
  list(key="mean_intensity", col="mean_intensity", logged=FALSE, ylab="Mean intensity (a.u.)",          title="PDF+ mean intensity")
)

# =============================================================================
# CORE: for one threshold, Welch test + brain-level group means, all metrics
# =============================================================================
analyze_threshold <- function(thr) {
  d <- df %>% filter(photoperiod=="SD", threshold==thr) %>% droplevels()
  stopifnot(nrow(d) == 16)

  welch_rows <- list(); mean_rows <- list()

  for (m in metrics) {
    col <- m$col

    # ---- brain-averaged values (unit of replication) ----
    bl <- d %>% group_by(brain_id, species) %>%
      summarise(value = mean(.data[[col]]), .groups="drop")

    vp <- bl$value[bl$species=="pipiens"]
    vq <- bl$value[bl$species=="quinquefasciatus"]

    # ---- Welch's t-test ----
    tt <- t.test(vp, vq, var.equal = FALSE)

    if (m$logged) {
      est   <- exp(mean(vp) - mean(vq))          # pip/quin ratio (fold-change)
      ci_lo <- exp(tt$conf.int[1]); ci_hi <- exp(tt$conf.int[2])
      elab  <- "fold-change (pip/quin)"
    } else {
      est   <- mean(vp) - mean(vq)               # difference
      ci_lo <- tt$conf.int[1]; ci_hi <- tt$conf.int[2]
      elab  <- "difference (pip - quin)"
    }

    welch_rows[[m$key]] <- data.frame(
      threshold=thr, metric=m$key,
      estimate=round(est,3), CI_low=round(ci_lo,3), CI_high=round(ci_hi,3),
      t=round(tt$statistic,3), df=round(tt$parameter,2),
      p_value=signif(tt$p.value,3), effect=elab, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

    # ---- brain-level group means (match the figure): mean +/- 1 SE (n=4) ----
    gm <- bl %>% group_by(species) %>%
      summarise(mlog = mean(value), se = sd(value)/sqrt(n()), .groups="drop") %>%
      mutate(estimate = if (m$logged) exp(mlog)      else mlog,
             lo       = if (m$logged) exp(mlog - se) else mlog - se,
             hi       = if (m$logged) exp(mlog + se) else mlog + se)

    mean_rows[[m$key]] <- data.frame(
      threshold=thr, metric=m$key, species=as.character(gm$species),
      estimate=round(gm$estimate,2),
      SE_band_low=round(gm$lo,2), SE_band_high=round(gm$hi,2),
      note=if(m$logged)"geometric mean, +/-1 SE (n=4 brains)" else "mean, +/-1 SE (n=4 brains)",
      stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  }

  list(welch=bind_rows(welch_rows), means=bind_rows(mean_rows), data=d)
}

results <- lapply(c("75","100","150"), analyze_threshold)
names(results) <- c("75","100","150")

welch_all <- bind_rows(lapply(results, `[[`, "welch"))
means_all <- bind_rows(lapply(results, `[[`, "means"))

# =============================================================================
# STATISTICS TABLES
# =============================================================================
write.csv(welch_all, "SD_stats_welch.csv", row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(means_all, "SD_stats_group_means.csv", row.names=FALSE)

# threshold-sensitivity view: effect + p for each metric across thresholds
sens_tbl <- welch_all %>%
  select(metric, threshold, estimate, CI_low, CI_high, p_value) %>%
  arrange(metric, threshold)
write.csv(sens_tbl, "SD_stats_threshold_sensitivity.csv", row.names=FALSE)

cat("\n===================== WELCH t-TEST (brain-averaged) =====================\n")
print(welch_all, row.names=FALSE)
cat("\n===================== GROUP MEANS (brain-level, match figures) ==========\n")
print(means_all, row.names=FALSE)
cat("\n===================== THRESHOLD SENSITIVITY =============================\n")
print(sens_tbl, row.names=FALSE)

# =============================================================================
# FIGURES — one bar plot per metric per threshold
#   bar     = group mean (geometric for area/CTCF; arithmetic for intensity)
#   error   = +/- 1 SE from the 4 brain values (back-transformed for logged)
#   points  = individual brains (n = 4 per species)
#   bracket = significance bracket connecting the two bars, labeled with
#             asterisks (* p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001, ns = not significant)
#             in place of a printed p-value
# =============================================================================
th_plot <- theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position="none",
        axis.text=element_text(color="black"),
        axis.text.x=element_text(face="italic"),
        plot.title=element_text(face="bold"),
        plot.subtitle=element_text(color="grey30"))

sp_cols <- c("Cx. pipiens"="#3B82B8", "Cx. quinquefasciatus"="#C65A1E")

# convert a p-value to conventional significance stars
get_stars <- function(p) {
  if (p < 0.001) return("***")
  if (p < 0.01)  return("**")
  if (p < 0.05)  return("*")
  return("ns")
}

make_barplot <- function(d, m, thr, welch_p) {
  col <- m$col

  pts <- d %>% group_by(brain_id, species) %>%
    summarise(val = if (m$logged) exp(mean(.data[[col]])) else mean(.data[[col]]),
              logmean = mean(.data[[col]]), .groups="drop") %>%
    mutate(species_lab = species_lab(species))

  gs <- pts %>% group_by(species) %>%
    summarise(mlog = mean(logmean), se = sd(logmean)/sqrt(n()), .groups="drop") %>%
    mutate(species_lab = species_lab(species),
           est = if (m$logged) exp(mlog)      else mlog,
           lo  = if (m$logged) exp(mlog - se) else mlog - se,
           hi  = if (m$logged) exp(mlog + se) else mlog + se)

  # headroom for the bracket + stars above the tallest point
  data_top    <- max(pts$val)
  plot_top    <- data_top * 1.38
  bracket_y   <- data_top * 1.12   # horizontal bar of the bracket
  tick_drop   <- data_top * 0.04   # length of the little downward ticks
  star_y      <- bracket_y + data_top * 0.11  # more clearance above the bracket

  stars <- get_stars(welch_p)

  ggplot(gs, aes(species_lab, est, fill=species_lab)) +
    geom_col(width=0.6, color="black") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=lo, ymax=hi), width=0.18) +
    geom_jitter(data=pts, aes(species_lab, val),
                width=0.10, height=0, size=2.6, shape=21, fill="white", color="black") +
    # significance bracket: two downward ticks + connecting horizontal line
    annotate("segment", x=1, xend=1, y=bracket_y - tick_drop, yend=bracket_y) +
    annotate("segment", x=2, xend=2, y=bracket_y - tick_drop, yend=bracket_y) +
    annotate("segment", x=1, xend=2, y=bracket_y, yend=bracket_y) +
    annotate("text", x=1.5, y=star_y, label=stars, size=5, fontface="bold") +
    scale_fill_manual(values=sp_cols) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0, plot_top)) +
    labs(title=m$title, subtitle=paste0("short day, threshold ", thr),
         x=NULL, y=m$ylab) + th_plot
}

for (thr in c("75","100","150")) {
  d  <- results[[thr]]$data
  wp <- results[[thr]]$welch
  for (m in metrics) {
    p <- make_barplot(d, m, thr, wp$p_value[wp$metric==m$key])
    ggsave(paste0("SD_", m$key, "_thr", thr, ".png"), p, width=4.2, height=4.2, dpi=300)
  }
}

cat("\nSaved figures: SD_<metric>_thr<75|100|150>.png  (9 total)\n")
cat("Saved tables : SD_stats_welch.csv, SD_stats_group_means.csv, SD_stats_threshold_sensitivity.csv\n")
```
